subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw core expose an opt-in per-engine deferred-maintenance timeout that releases the session lane and fences late plugin side effects, rather than continue relying on the existing session-level/compaction safety boundaries?
rationale: The implementation preserves upgrades by default, but selecting a new operator-configured timeout and defining the host-versus-plugin lifecycle boundary is a product and compatibility contract, not a narrow mechanical repair.

options.title: Accept the opt-in core boundary
options.body: Keep the new disabled-by-default setting and fence contract, then require a rebase and exact-head validation before merge.

options.title: Use an existing timeout policy
options.body: Reject the new setting and redesign the fix around an existing compaction or session safety timeout if maintainers want one canonical operator control.

options.title: Keep timeout ownership in plugins
options.body: Decline the core timeout/fence policy and require context-engine plugins to bound their own maintenance work through an existing plugin contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the opt-in core boundary
recommendation.body: Keep the new disabled-by-default setting and fence contract, then require a rebase and exact-head validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their adjacent proposal directly analyzed the timeout and late-side-effect boundary this decision must settle.
